abstract: Objectives: Acute nutritional interventions may modulate cognitive function and underlying brain activity. This study investigated the impact of consuming three kiwifruit varieties - green (Zespri Green), gold (Zespri SunGold), and red (Zespri RubyRed) - on cognitive performance and brain activation using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Methods: Fourteen healthy participants completed a randomized, repeated-measures study involving four MRI sessions following consumption of each kiwifruit type and a maltodextrin control. Cognitive function was assessed using an N-back working memory task during fMRI acquisition. Behavioural performance, psychometric measures (mood, fatigue, appetite), and blood biomarkers (vitamin C) were also collected. Results: Kiwifruit consumption significantly increased plasma vitamin C levels relative to control, with peak concentrations observed at 100 minutes post-consumption. Behaviourally, task difficulty increased with N-back load, while psychometric measures indicated greater positive affect following kiwifruit compared to control. fMRI results showed that the maltodextrin condition elicited broader brain activation, suggesting reduced neural efficiency. In contrast, kiwifruit -particularly the red variety - showed enhanced differentiation between low and high cognitive load (2-back vs. 0-back), with increased activation in regions associated with working memory and cognitive control. Conclusions: These findings suggest that acute kiwifruit consumption may enhance cognitive efficiency and modulate brain responses, with effects varying by kiwifruit cultivar.
